segments.text: The goal is the level6 password from /levels/level5: another unbounded strcpy of our argument into a stack buffer, with the same no-randomization posture as level four.
The source and objdump show the same vulnerable shape as level four, so the same shellcode strategy applies: get the ids aligned with setreuid, then execve bin slash sh.
I open vim and write the shellcode with the level-five ids, assemble it with nasm, and extract the raw bytes.
I open vim and write the exploit, riding the environment for a stable landing address, and fire it at the level.
The run lands in the shellcode and the shell reads the pass file: ur underscore so underscore l33t.
